newsitem.title: UK: Any German withdrawal could cloud CW strategy.
newsitem.headline: Any German withdrawal could cloud CW strategy.

text.p: Any divorce of Cable and Wireless Plc (C&W) and German industrial conglomerate Veba AG may yield short-term benefits -- but it hangs a question mark over the British telecoms group's European strategy.

Some investment bankers and analysts said they sympathised with C&W executives, who were expected on Thursday to remain behind closed doors, locked in talks with Veba about the future of their joint ventures in Germany and other European countries.

But some questioned the group's apparent change of strategy, based on a lower risk, lower reward principle that shies away from vast infrastructure investments in Germany -- investments which might not generate attractive returns on capital.

"If they exit (the Veba venture) at a sensible price...it's going to have an earnings-enhancing effect because they won't have their share of start-up losses," said one investment banker, who declined to be named.
"But by and large, you've got to be very careful to distinguish between the short-term presentational benefit and the longer-term strategic issue."

Unless C&W seals a deal with an international carrier such as Global One, which incorporates Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp, some said the group's European strategy could be in doubt if it abandoned its German venture, which is dubbed Vebacom.
Germany is seen as one of the cornerstones of the European telecoms market.

But C&W lacks a cohesive set of mobile telephone investments in Europe and most analysts agreed that shunting voice and data down telephone lines leased from dominant telecoms operators, who would then determine C&W's cost base, was not the way to enter a market effectively.

Although the cost of leased lines is expected to fall as competition in Europe starts to bite around 1998, investors are concerned that the regulatory regimes in key markets such as Germany and France might favour dominant national players.
"C&W would end up losing less money (by not investing in infrastructure) -- but might not create a real business," the investment banker noted.
"If you hypothesise, a Vebacom withdrawal could mean C&W is effectively withdrawing from the continental European market."

But there are alternative approaches. America's MFS Communication Co MFST.O builds fibre optic rings around major cities, offers services including data traffic, markets aggressively, cherry picks the best customers from dominant phone firms and rolls that out across Europe.

Andrew Harrington, telecoms analyst at brokers Salomon Bros, says C&W will probably just link up Global One, whose key rivals are British Telecommunications and MCI's Concert alliance and America's AT&T.

"I don't think anything is imminent. But I think they will do something with Global One. I think their European strategy will be part of a global strategy to fill in their gaps in asset coverage," he said.
C&W has large gaps in its asset base in America and Europe -- but has a significant asset base in Britain and Asia, via a majority holding in Hong Kong Telecommunications.

"I think the main conclusion of a pullout from Vebacom is that C&W have accepted that they haven't got the resources to be a global carrier by themselves. So they have to team up with somebody," Harrington said.
"C&W and Global One were meant for each other," he added.
